qt: to the Commission António Tânger Corrêa (PfE), Elisabeth Dieringer (PfE), Susanna Ceccardi (PfE), Hermann Tertsch (PfE), Sebastian Kruis (PfE), Alvise Pérez (NI), Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE) Subject:
Judicial independence and democratic safeguards in Brazil under the EU– Mercosur Agreement

Following Brazil’s presidential elections of 25 October 2026, Brasil’s Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin ordered a two-hour extension of voting, subsequently limited to polling stations still open. On 26 October, Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered opposition candidate Flávio Bolsonaro to surrender his passports and prohibited him from leaving Brazil. Although the Partido Liberal formally recognised the electoral results, these decisions raise serious concerns regarding judicial impartiality, proportionality, due process and the protection of political opposition. Respect for democracy, fundamental rights and the rule of law constitute an essential element of the EU–Mercosur framework. We therefore ask: 1.
Will the Commission conduct an independent assessment of these judicial interventions, particularly regarding judicial impartiality, proportionality and opposition rights?
Will the Commission request formal explanations from Brazilian authorities concerning the legal grounds for extending voting hours and restricting Flávio Bolsonaro’s freedom of movement?

Will the Commission initiate a formal assessment of Brazil’s compliance with its democratic and rule of law obligations and commit to initiating the procedures under Article 23.6 of the EU-Mercosur interim Trade Agreement, including the possible suspension of the Agreement?
